literal: At the time of ruin they shrink not, the strong-willed; by a mass of arrows having been struck, standing firm in greatness, the bull elephant.
translation: The strong-willed will not lose heart when facing defeat. They are like a bull elephant that stands firm in its greatness even when struck by a shower of arrows.
modern: தோல்வி வந்தாலும் மன உறுதி உடையவர்கள் மனம் தளர மாட்டார்கள். அவர்கள், உடம்பில் அம்புகள் பாய்ந்தாலும் தன் பெருமை குன்றாமல் உறுதியாக நிற்கும் ஆண் யானையைப் போன்றவர்கள்.
explanation: This couplet compares strong-willed people to a majestic bull elephant in battle. Even when pierced by a thick shower of arrows, the elephant does not fall but stands firm in its pride. Similarly, those with true inner strength will not lose their motivation or shrink back when they face ruin or severe setbacks. The word 'பாடு' here carries the sense of greatness or dignity, showing how the elephant, and the strong-willed person, maintain their stature in adversity.
